title: append and insert
goal: This lesson covers how to grow a list by adding items at the end with append, or at a chosen spot with insert.
learn: append() adds an item at the end
insert() adds an item at an index
The list gets longer after each add
idea: append(value) sticks a new item on the end of the list. insert(index, value) slides a new item in at that index and shifts the later items to the right. Firstly you give it the index, and after that the value, and mixing those two up is an easy mistake to make.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change tasks.append("walk dog") to tasks.append("call mum") and press Run. The second printed list should end with call mum.

practice.text: Start with two snacks. Append one more, then print the list.
practice.hint: Call append on the snacks list with one new snack name in quotes. append adds to the end.
practice.starterTip: Try snacks.append("cookie") or any third snack, then print(snacks).
practice.starter:
snacks = ["chips", "apple"]
# Append a third snack

print(snacks)
practice.gradingNote: Pass if append adds a third item and the list is printed with three items.

practice.text: Insert "start" at index 0 of the list, then print.
practice.hint: insert takes two arguments, the index first and then the value. Index 0 is the front of the list.
practice.starterTip: Add steps.insert(0, "start") under the comment, then print(steps).
practice.starter:
steps = ["middle", "end"]
# Insert at the front

print(steps)
practice.gradingNote: Pass if insert(0, "start") is used and the list begins with start.

quiz.question: What does items.append("x") do?
quiz.correct: Right, append always adds to the end.
quiz.wrong: append puts the new item after the last existing item.

quiz.question: After a = [1, 3] and a.insert(1, 2), what is a?
quiz.wrong: The first argument is the index and the second is the value.

quiz.question: How does the list length change after one append?
quiz.correct: Right, each append adds one item, so len goes up by 1.
quiz.wrong: Adding an item increases the length by one.
